questions.question: An EEG is a test used to evaluate the electrical activity in the brain. Select the full form of EEG.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electroencephalogram.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• EEG stands for** Electroencephalogram.**
 
• An EEG is used to **detect problems in the electrical activity of the brain** that may be associated with certain** brain disorders.**
 
• The measurements given by an EEG are used to confirm various conditions including **head injury, epilepsy, brain tumor, memory problems, stroke, sleep disorders.**
 
• Brain cells communicate with each other through **electrical impulses.**
 
• An EEG **tracks and records brain wave patterns.**
 
• Small flat metal discs called electrodes are attached to the scalp with wires.
 
• The electrodes analyze the **electrical impulses in the brain and send signals to a computer that records the results.**
 
• The electrical impulses in an EEG recording look like **wavy lines with peaks and valleys.**
 
• These lines allow **doctors to quickly assess** whether there are abnormal patterns.
 
• Any irregularities may be a **sign of seizures or other brain disorders.**

questions.question: _______ states that temperature and other physical conditions remaining the same, the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ohm’s law.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Ohm’s law states that temperature and other physical conditions remaining the same, the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
 
• **Voltage = Current × Resistance**
 
 
• V = I × R
 
 
 
• **V = voltage, I = current and R = resistance**
 
• The SI unit of resistance is ohms and is denoted by Ω.
 
• It helps to calculate the power, efficiency, current, voltage, and resistance of an element of an electrical circuit.
 
• It an element follows the ohm’s law, then the element is known as a linear element.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Coulomb's Law
 It states that two stationary point charges attract or repel each other with a force that is directly proportional to the product of the magnitude of charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
 
 

 Hooke's Law
 According to this law within the elastic limits, the stress is directly proportional to the strain produced in a body.
 
 

 Pascals Law
 It states that if the effect of gravity is neglected, the pressure at every point of liquid in equilibrium or rest is the same.
 
 

 Stefan's Law
 According to this law, the amount of heat radiated by unit area of the surface in one second is directly proportional to the fourth power of absolute temperature of the body

questions.question: The weight of an object of mass 1 kg is approximately equal to ______ newton.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• While mass is a measure of the amount of matter in an object, weight is the force of gravity that is acting on an object of a given mass.
 
• As we know,
 
• ** Force = Mass × Acceleration**
 
• Therefore, Weight (W) = Mass (m) × Acceleration due to gravity (g)
 
• ** So, the weight of an object of mass 1 kg = 1 × 10 = 10 N (g = 10 m/s2)**

questions.question: Which of the following laws deduces the expression for the force between two stationary point charges in vacuum or free space?
questions.solution:
​The correct answer is __**Coulomb’s Law.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Coulomb’s Law talks about the magnitude of the attraction between the two charges.

 
 
• It says that the force is directly proportional to the product of the quantity of the two charges.
 
• F ∝ q1q2, where (F is Force, q1 and q2 are charges).
 
• It is also inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
 
 
 
• i.e., F ∝ 1/r2 where (F is Force, r is the distance between the charges).
 
• Thus, the equation is
 
• F = k({{q₁)/(q₂)}}{{{r₂}}} where k is the proportionality constant and is equal to 9 × 109 Nm2/C2.
 
• The Law was given by Charles-Augustin de Coulomb in the year 1784.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Lenz's law states that the direction of the induced current in the coil will be always in such a way that it opposes the change which produces the current.
 
• According to **Gauss law,** the total electric flux linked with a closed surface called Gaussian surface is (1)/(ϵ_o) the charge enclosed by the closed surface.
 
• **Ohm’s law** states that at a constant temperature, the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.

questions.question: Lactometers, hydrometers, ships and submarines are designed on ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Archimedes' principle.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The upward buoyant force that is exerted on a body immersed in a fluid, whether partially or fully submerged, is equal to the weight of the fluid that the body displaces and acts in the upward direction at the center of mass of the displaced fluid.
 
• The value of thrust force is given by the Archimedes law which Archimedes of Syracuse of Greece discovered.
 
• When an object is partially or fully immersed in a liquid, the apparent loss of weight is equal to the weight of the liquid displaced by it.
 
• Lactometers, hydrometers, ships, and submarines are designed on this principle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The principle of gravitation:**

 
 
• Newton’s law of universal gravitation states that any particle of matter in the universe attracts another one with a force varying directly as the product of the masses and inversely as the square of the distance between them.
 
 
 
• **The Principle of relative density:**
 
 
• The difference between the specific gravity and density is that at room temperature and pressure, 1gram per 1 cubic cm is the density of water this density is treated as a standard and the density of any other material (usual liquids) is calculated relative to this is called relative density or specific gravity.
 
 
 
• **principle of buoyancy:**
 
 
• The principle states that the buoyant force acting on an object immersed in or floating on a fluid is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by the object.

questions.question: Which of the following laws can be explained as 'An object remains in a state of rest or of uniform motion in a straight line unless compelled to change that state by an applied force.'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**First law of motion.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• First law of motion can explained as 'An object remains in a state of rest or of uniform motion in a straight line unless compelled to change that state by an applied force.'
 
• The first law of newton implies that things cannot stop, start or change direction all by themselves.
 
• The things require some outside force.
 
• This property to resist changes of massive bodies in their state of motion is called inertia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Second Law of newton states that the force acting on the body is equal to the product of its acceleration and mass.
 
• The Third Law of Newton states that for every action there is an opposite and equal reaction.
 
• The first law of thermodynamics only gives information about the energy balance when a system undergoes a change of state.
 
 
• But it does not help to predict whether the change of state is feasible or not.

questions.question: Which law explains about the tides due to the moon and the sun?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Law of gravitation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The gravitational attraction between two bodies **is directly proportional to their masses and inversely proportional to the square of their distance, according to **Newton's law of universal gravitation.**
 
• As a result, the gravitational attraction between two things increases as their mass increases and their distance decreases.
 
• The main force that causes tides is gravity.** Sir Isaac Newton** explained in 1687 that ocean tides are caused by the sun and moon's gravitational force on the earth's oceans.
 
• The gravitational attractive force is what causes tidal forces. The distance between two objects is frequently more important than their masses when it comes to tidal pressures on Earth.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The angle of the reflected** ray is equal to the angle of the incident ray when reflected off a smooth surface with respect to the normal to the surface, which is a line perpendicular to the surface at the point of contact, according to **the law of reflection**.
 
• **Law of refraction: **At the point of incidence, the incident ray refracted ray, and normal to the interface of two media all lie on the same plane.
 
• **The law of inertia, **commonly known as Newton's first law, states that if a body is at rest or moving in a straight line at a constant speed, it will remain at rest or continue to move in a straight path at constant speed until it is acted with by a force.

questions.question: Which of the following instruments is used to detect and record earthquakes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seismograph**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A seismograph is an instrument used to record the **vibrations of an earthquake**.
 
• It's an instrument consists a **vibrating rod, or a pendulum**, which starts vibrating when tremors occur.
 
• A pen is attached to the vibrating system of the seismograph which** records seismic waves** on paper which

 moves under it.
 
• The **first seismograph** was invented in **132 AD by Chinese astronomer and mathematician Zhang Heng**.
 
• The **magnitude of the earthquake** is measured on the **Richter scale** while its **intensity** on the **Mercalli scale**.
 
• The **magnitude relates** to the** energy released during the quake** and the **intensity scale** takes into account the **visible damage caused by the event**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 Electric current

questions.question: The size of the pupil of the eye is controlled by the _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**iris**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **iris** regulates the amount of light entering the eyes.
 
• Iris is the **coloured part of the eye that gives pigment to the eye.**
 
• It is attached to ciliary muscles which will contract and expand to accommodate light in required amounts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ab0ae76cdf1612f33c129a616a40343105045de0698905bece80fe8f1f98bff8.png] 

 
• The **cornea** is the outermost layer of the eye and focuses the entry of light into the eye.
 
• ​A **pupil** is a dark circle located at the centre of the iris. It will adjust itself to the amount of light entering the eye.
 
• The** eye lens **adjusts its shape and thickness as required to help focus on the retina.
 
• The** retina** is the light-sensitive membrane behind the eye where the image is formed.
 
• The **visual signals **regarding the image formed are transmitted to the brain in the form of electrical signals through the optic nerves.

questions.question: The instrument used to measure either direct or alternating electric current in amperes is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ammeter.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• An **ammeter **is an instrument that is used to measure either direct or alternating **electric current** in amperes.
 
• It has a set of coils with very low resistance and inductive reactance.
 
• This allows for very low impedance, the force that opposes electric current.
 
• An ammeter can measure a wide range of current values because at high values only a small portion of the current is directed through the meter mechanism; a shunt in parallel with the meter carries the major portion of the current.​

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Accelerometer:**

 
 
• ​An accelerometer is a device that** measures the vibration, or acceleration of motion of a structure.**
 
• The main working principle of an accelerometer is that it converts mechanical energy into electrical energy.
 
• When a mass is kept on the sensor which is actually just like a spring it starts moving down. Since it is moving down it starts experiencing acceleration.
 
 
 
• **Barometer:**
 
 
• A barometer is a scientific instrument used to measure** atmospheric pressure**, also called barometric pressure.
 
• Inventor: **Evangelista Torricelli.**
 
 
 
• **Voltmeter:​**
 
 
• ​A voltmeter is an instrument used for measuring the **electric potential **difference between two points in an electric circuit.
 
• It is connected in parallel.
 
• It usually has high resistance so that it takes negligible current from the circuit.

__
 
• **The gnomon is the part of a sundial that casts the shadow.**
 
• It is probably also the** world's oldest astronomical instrument.**
 
• It is like a** pole stuck in the sand.**
 
• It has been** used to measure the passage of time by nomadic cultures of the Sahara for centuries.**
 
• The gnomon may be **a rod, wire, or elaborately decorated metal casting.**
 
• **It has to be parallel to the axis of the Earth's rotation for the sundial** to be accurate throughout the year.

• **Telescope**

 
 
• **​Used to form magnified images of distant objects.**
 
• **Most important investigative instrument in astronomy.**
 
• **Galileo **applied the **telescope to the study of extraterrestrial bodies.**
 
 
 
• **Transformer **
 
 
• An **electrical device designed to convert alternating current from one voltage to another.**
 
• It can be** designed to "step up" or "step down" voltages.**
 
• Works on the** magnetic induction principle.**
 
 
 
• **Bolometer**
 
 
• ​The bolometer is a device **used for detecting and measuring the heat and radiation of Microwave energy or RF.**
 
• It **uses the temperature-sensitive resistive element** whose resistance changes with the temperature.
 
• The** Thermistor and Barretter are examples** of the commonly used resistive element.

questions.question: In a photovoltaic cell which type of energy gets converted into electrical energy?

• This consists of a** p-n junction **formed by **gaseous diffusion **near the front surface of a **silicon plate.**

• A **Solar Photovoltaic cell is a semiconductor **system made of **silicon** or similar materials.

questions.question: Scattering of a beam of light by a medium containing small suspended particles is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tyndall effect**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Tyndall effect: It is also known as Tyndall scattering. The scattering of light by particles in a colloid or else particles in a very fine suspension is called Tyndall effect.
 
• Under this effect, the longer wavelength light is more transmitted while the shorter wavelength light is more reflected.
 
• Scattering of light: The phenomenon in which the light ray is redirected in all other directions on passing through particles of dimensions comparable to the wavelength of the light used is called scattering of light.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ba487883bb65b877213a6ca2b4be7d182460bdd42a272f2a0179839ab2b11db4.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Tyndall scattering occurs when the dimensions of the particles that are causing the scattering are larger than the wavelength of the scattered radiation.
 
• This effect is used to determine whether a mixture is a true solution or a colloid.
 
• Milk, starch solution, and emulsions show the Tyndall effect whereas sugar solution doesn’t show the Tyndall effect.

questions.question: Which among the following is used as a reflector in search lights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Concave mirror.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Concave mirror is used as a reflector in search lights.
 
• Concave mirror: The mirrors curved inside on the reflecting side are called concave mirrors.
 
 
• These mirrors produce real as well as virtual images, inverted and erect, and magnified as well as the diminished image of the object.
 
• These are used in:
 
• reflecting telescope, 
 
• shaving mirrors, 
 
• ophthalmoscopes
 
• reflector for the headlight of a vehicle and
 
• searchlights.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Convex mirror: It is an outward curved mirror that produces a diminished image.

 
 
• Convex mirrors either diverge a parallel beam of light into all directions or gather light from all directions and produce a parallel beam out of it.
 
• Convex mirrors are used as rear view mirrors in vehicles, sunglasses, magnifying glasses.
 
• Convex mirrors are those which have the bulging side facing the light.
 
 
 
• **Concave lenses** are most commonly used to correct myopia which is also called near-sightedness. 
 
• **A plane mirror** has several different uses and applications, including periscope and kaleidoscope, automobiles, shaving mirrors, dentists' mirror, torch lights, solar cookers, and security-related purposes.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true about nuclear fusion?

options.text: It produces much more energy than nuclear fission
The process is used for making nuclear bomb.
Electricity production through this process is commercially less viable than nuclear fission.
It is the source of energy in the stars.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e., **__The process is used for making nuclear bomb__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **A nuclear bomb** uses either uranium or plutonium and relies on **fission, **a nuclear reaction in which **a nucleus or an atom breaks into two pieces.**
 
• The by-products of nuclear fission include free neutrons, photons usually in the form of** gamma rays,** and other atomic fragments such as **beta particles and alpha particles.**
 
• Nuclear fission produces energy for nuclear power and drives atomic weapon explosions**.**
 
• **Nuclear fusion** is a reaction in which two or more atomic nuclei are combined to form one or more different atomic nuclei and subatomic particles (neutrons or protons).
 
• **An example **of nuclear fusion is the process of four hydrogens coming together to form helium.
 
• **A hydrogen bomb **is based on the principle of uncontrollable nuclear fusion.

The correct answer is __**Potentiometer.**__

__
 
• Potentiometers work by varying the position of a sliding contact across a uniform resistance.
 
• In a potentiometer, the entire input voltage is applied across the whole length of the resistor, and the output voltage is the voltage drop between the fixed and sliding contact.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are two main types of potentiometers, linear potentiometers, and rotary potentiometers.
 
 
• Membrane Potentiometers are another type of potentiometer.
 
• They are often referred to as “soft spots” and can be either linear or rotary.
 
• The principle of a potentiometer is that the **potential dropped across a segment of a wire of uniform cross-section** carrying a constant current is directly proportional to its length.
 
• The potentiometer is a simple device used **to measure the electrical potentials(or compare the e.m.f of a cell).**
